title: Zugzwang as a tactical weapon
summary: The Immortal Zugzwang game, waiting moves, and endgame positions where passing the move wins.

steps.md:
## When every move is a concession

**Zugzwang**: the side to move would prefer to pass, because every legal move worsens its position. Most common in endgames (king and pawn, queen v rook), but also in middlegames where one side's pieces are completely tied up.

How to use it: (1) make sure your own position has **spare moves** (pawn moves, a free king or bishop move), (2) restrict the opponent's useful moves one by one, (3) then make a **waiting move** and let him self-destruct.

**Saemisch-Nimzowitsch, Copenhagen 1923, after 25.Rce1.** Black's pieces dominate the light squares and the f-file; White has almost no safe moves. Nimzowitsch played **25...h6!!**, a pure waiting move, and White **resigned**: every white move loses material (a bishop move drops a piece, Kh2 allows ...R5f3, a rook move on the back rank allows ...Rxd2/...Bxb1, and so on). Engine: Black is about +6 after h6 and after several other quiet moves — the point is that White has no useful move at all.

steps.question: In the Saemisch-Nimzowitsch position, why is 25...h6 strong although it creates no new threat?
choices: It is a waiting move: all of White's moves lose material, so passing the move wins
It protects the king from back-rank mate only
steps.explain: This is zugzwang in the middlegame. The waiting move also gives the black king luft, removing the last back-rank worry.

steps.prompt: Queen against knight pawn on the 7th. White to move and win (tablebase).
steps.explain: **1.Qb1!** blockades the pawn on the promotion square at once; Black's king must step away from b2's protection and the white king walks in. Other moves also win but take much longer (tablebase: 1.Qb1 mates in 10, the next best in 17).

steps.question: Which statement about zugzwang in practical play is correct?
choices: It only occurs in pawn endings
Keep spare tempi (pawn moves you can make without weakening) because in tense positions the side that runs out of useful moves loses
Zugzwang is impossible when queens are on the board
The side with more material can never be in zugzwang
steps.explain: Spare tempi decide many endgames and some middlegames. Queens and rooks on the board make zugzwang rarer but not impossible (Saemisch-Nimzowitsch had queens and rooks).
